One taller narrow teal-roof house should reach up to about x60% / y12% of the full image, another red-roof house around x67% / y20%. 2. Keep the LOWER TWO LOBES as a huge dense ship carpet, but move the LEFTMOST bows and yards at the height of the lower-left fleet about 7% of canvas width INWARD TO THE RIGHT. Below halfway down, no boat/mast/foam should project into x0–22% of canvas; the full LEFT outline must step RIGHT there as in the diagram. Hide at least its lower TWO THIRDS behind foreground rock/trees. The ridge/peak must remain the dominant height. Keep a faint snowy path wrapping around the mountain and disappearing behind it toward that tower.
Retain the gateway's compact stone steps -> rope ladder -> two-storey tavern -> rear bridge route at the southeast end. Sparse irregular underrooms, tall uneven grey trestles, different suspension bridges. Warm chestnut and walnut boat hulls with occasional worn muted green/red planks; cool town timber. Keep all ship sails furled or heavily gathered, little irregular bundles with rope ties; no big deployed sail triangles, no identical horizontal sausage bars.
Entire artwork complete with organic natural ends. No straight sliced cutoffs, clipping, geometric borders, guide shapes, words or labels. ACTUAL TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND. Same 856:680 aspect ratio, high-resolution watercolor adventure-book painting. Preserve the current chaotic fleet character strongly.
